thread:
raj: Heads up — noticed a customer hit a hard schema validation reject on a function/tool call and got a 400 with no fallback. Billing shows token charge but no usable output. Anyone else seeing a spike?
megan: Seen a couple. Can you paste the error payload?
raj: Paste from logs: ```{"request_id":"req_9X","route":"tool-invoke","error":"SchemaValidationError","detail":"expected object but got array","model":"gpt-xx-1"}```
oliver: That error screams strict validation toggle. We rolled strictToolValidation to 30% for the canary last night.
sasha: If strict validation rejects before adapter fallback, apps get a 400 instead of routed fallback — UX is rough and customers get billed. Need to decide whether reject should trigger permissive fallback path. :thinking_face:
megan: Can we add sampling for the full payload when rejects happen? Current telemetry only sends counts, not the offending JSON, so rollouts are blind.
console-bot: deploybot: strictToolValidation rollout started 2024-11-03T02:12:00Z -> 30% traffic.
anna: (cc @megan) Billing team flagged two invoices where tokens were charged but customer got no response. They want a mitigation now.
oliver: Proposed quick fix: flip strictToolValidation back to 10% and enable permissive-fallback-on-reject for 1h while we gather samples. That avoids immediate 400s for most traffic.
raj: +1 flip now. We should also capture a 1% trace sampling of full request/response for rejected calls (PII redacted) so QA can triage shapes.
sasha: UX request for Console: surface a per-route "schema rejects" column in the model dashboard and expose sample payloads (redacted) with one-click download. We currently only have aggregate counts.
megan: I'll file an infra task for sampling + console surface. Can someone flip the toggle for the rollback?
oliver: I'll flip to 10% in the rollout service now and open a rollback PR. Doing it in 2 mins. :wrench:
console-bot: deploybot: strictToolValidation adjusted: 30% -> 10% (actor: oliver)
raj: After rollback, let's confirm affected customers auto-retry via permissive adapter route. If not, we need a short-lived proxy that maps rejects to permissive-run with a rejection header.
anna: I'll work with billing to mark the flagged invoices pending until we confirm remediation.
megan: Follow-ups: (1) sampling pipeline task (2) console dashboard column (3) decision doc on whether rejects should ever be billed. I'll own 1 and 2; oliver/raj to own decision doc.
oliver: Agree. Will start the decision doc draft.
raj: Thanks everyone. Quick wins: rollback + 1% sampling + console alert. Longer term: change rejection flow so it never returns 400 to end user without clear fallback. :+1:
megan: tagging @product for prioritization of the decision doc and console UX.
sasha: Also add an eval set that triggers the reject for canary monitoring. We need automated alerts for spikes in schema rejects.
raj: Perfect. I'll DM the impacted customer with ETA.
